title: Dragnet
paragraphs: NBC police procedural based on actual LAPD cases and developed around documentary realism. Frozen GRH snapshot has 293 objects from July 7, 1949 through October 30, 1956, including four post-final-new-production reruns.

GRH documents the program through Joe Friday / Ben Romero new-production era (June 3, 1949 to December 13, 1951) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], Partner-transition era (December 27, 1951 to September 14, 1952) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], Joe Friday / Frank Smith new-production era (September 21, 1952 to September 20, 1955) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], and NBC rerun era (September 27, 1955 to February 26, 1957) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]].

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are [[person|jack-webb|Jack Webb]] (performer on 274 recordings and producer on 2 recordings), Ben Alexander (performer on 141 recordings and writer on 1 recording), George Fenneman (announcer on 101 recordings and commercial spokesman on 3 recordings), Barton Yarborough (performer on 100 recordings), Walter Schumann (music on 53 recordings, conductor on 30 recordings, announcer on 1 recording, performer on 1 recording, and writer on 1 recording), Hal Gibney (announcer on 53 recordings and host on 27 recordings), and John Robinson (writer on 52 recordings).

The program is also connected in the archive to [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]] (broadcast on network), [[org|org.cd82fd99edb39caa|Armed Forces Radio and Television Service]] (rebroadcast by), and [[org|org.4798d1172deaae2c|Armed Forces Radio Service]] (rebroadcast by).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include robbery and burglary, homicide investigation, juvenile crime and welfare, domestic and family crisis, missing persons and kidnapping, and police procedure and investigation.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including Postwar urban policing and procedural realism, Police technical cooperation in mass-media drama, and Radio-to-television transition.
